_comment: STUB (2026-08-31). Catalogue of Antelope mic-modelling ('emuMic') models for the Orion Studio III's per-preamp mic emulation. This file is intentionally separate from the device profile: the model list a given user can actually load depends on which Antelope modelling mic + model packs are registered to THEIR Antelope account, so a client should pick a model set per user, not per device. The DEVICE-SIDE control of the modelling DSP (enable / polar pattern / capsule swap) is in profiles/orion_studio_3.json -> frame.micmodeling_command + params.mic_modeling; THIS file is only about the model-selection layer.
status: model list captured 2026-08-31 for ONE account (Edge Duo owner); IDs may be list-position, not global -- see models._comment. Per-model polar-pattern index ranges swept 2026-09-01 (macos-emumic-polar-patterns).

what_is_known.dsp_control_frame: opcode 0x17 / param_id 0xe5 (frame.micmodeling_command in orion_studio_3.json). Frame: e5 05 <ch> <enabled> <model> <swap> <pattern>. [20] = model id (0 = EdgeDuo / raw), [22] = polar-pattern INDEX (0-based) -- with model 0 it is the free 0-100 morph (0 omni / 50 cardioid / 100 fig-8); with a selected model it is a small index into that model's pattern list (range per model, see models[].patterns). Selecting a model presets [22] to that model's DEFAULT index (the value formerly called 'pattern_class' -- 0 for fixed, 1 for the 3-way mics, 4 for the 9-detent mics). Present on preamps 5-12 (8 channels); the EMU button shows per channel only in Mic mode (corrected 2026-09-03 -- was 7-12; emumic 5/6 route+read-back on the device and channel_bias -4 puts [18]=0 at preamp 5).
what_is_known.matrix_source: the modelled (wet) signal is routing source bank 0x01 ('emumic'), idx 0-7 = preamps 5-12 (confirmed 2026-08-31, capture 'emumic-5to 12'). Distinct from bank 0x00 (dry preamp).
what_is_known.model_selection_frame: SAME frame as the DSP control (0x17/0xe5), byte [20] = model id. Captured 2026-08-31 ('emumic-model-select-...', 18 models cycled). On select, [22] is preset to the model's default pattern index. No readback -- write-only.
what_is_known.polar_pattern_sweep: macos-emumic-polar-patterns (2026-09-01): every model 0..18 selected on preamps 7-8 and its polar-pattern UI control clicked through. [22] is the pattern index and its observed range is per-model (models[].patterns). [21] channel-swap and [23]/[24] stayed 0 throughout. Enabling still fires one SET_LINK for the preamp pair. Models 1/12/16/18 (Tokyo 800T, Berlin M251/K86/47 TU) only had indices 0 and 1 exercised -- whether they also have index 2 is unconfirmed (their default index is 1, which for the 3-way mics is the middle position, so a third value is plausible; re-sweep to settle).
what_is_known.side_effects_of_enabling: the Launcher also turns on 48V phantom (param 0x51) for the pair and links the preamp pair (SET_LINK space 0).

pattern_class._comment: PARTIALLY CORRECTED 2026-09-01. This is the [22] value the Launcher presets when a model is selected -- it is the model's DEFAULT polar-pattern INDEX, not a separate class code (macos-emumic-polar-patterns showed [22] is always the pattern index). It still works as a rough family label because the default sits in the middle of the range: 0 => a single fixed pattern (control locked); 1 => a switchable mic, default = cardioid (models 3/4/7 confirmed 3-way 0/1/2; models 1/12/16/18 only 0/1 seen); 4 => a 9-detent multipattern mic, default = cardioid, index 0..8 (models 9/10/11). Kept under the old key name to avoid churn in this stub; see models[].patterns for the per-model observed range.
pattern_class.0: fixed single pattern (the modelled mic's native one -- e.g. a FET cardioid or a ribbon figure-8; the pattern control is locked at index 0)
pattern_class.1: switchable, default index 1 (cardioid). Confirmed 3-way (0 omni / 1 cardioid / 2 fig-8) for models 3, 4, 7; models 1, 12, 16, 18 had only 0 and 1 exercised.
pattern_class.4: 9-detent multipattern, default index 4 (cardioid), full range 0..8 (omni -> fig-8). Models 9, 10, 11.

pattern_index_ranges_2026_09_01._comment: byte [22] values observed per model in macos-emumic-polar-patterns (preamps 7-8, all 19 models). Index, not degrees. Model 0 is the exception: 0-100 continuous morph.
pattern_index_ranges_2026_09_01.0: 0-100 continuous (Edge Duo raw morph; 0 omni / 50 cardioid / 100 fig-8)

account_binding.note: Antelope Edge / Verge modelling mics and the model/emulation packs are activated online against an Antelope account. A model the user does not own will not load. A client should therefore let the user declare which mic(s) + packs they have (or, better, read the entitlement list if that ever proves reachable -- it is NOT reachable from the HID interface, which has no readback at all) and only offer those models.
account_binding.do_not: do not ship the licensed emulation model list scraped from Antelope's software, and never touch activation/entitlement traffic -- same policy as the AFX plugin chain (see CLAUDE.md 'AFX / Synergy Core plugins -- plan of attack', buckets E/F).

modelling_mics._comment: The Antelope modelling-mic hardware families. capsules / pattern_control / the mic descriptions are public product-page facts. `confirmed` and `requires_pair` are OUR findings: `confirmed` = the Orion emuMic behaviour was exercised against the device WITH this mic -- true only for the Edge Duo (every emuMic capture on file -- emumic-model-select, macos-emumic-polar-patterns, macos-ch7-8-micmodeling-* -- was on an Edge Duo account; the model list, polar-morph range and channel swap all come from those). The single-capsule mics are untested here, so a client should offer only the confirmed one(s). `requires_pair` = enabling emuMic occupies BOTH preamps of a modeling-capable pair (5-6 / 7-8 / 9-10 / 11-12): the captures show enable emitting SET_LINK for the pair (space 0) and the mic-modeling params written twice, [18]=N then [18]=N+1 (see params.mic_modeling.notes / what_is_known.side_effects_of_enabling). For the Edge Duo that matches its hardware -- two capsules on two XLRs -- so the pair must be linked and both channels carry the same model/pattern.

edge_solo.notes: single large-diaphragm modelling mic. Orion emuMic behaviour with this mic: untested.

edge_duo.notes: dual-capsule; occupies a linked preamp PAIR (5-6 / 7-8 / 9-10 / 11-12 -- any modeling-capable pair). The continuous polar-pattern morph (byte [22], 0 omni / 50 cardioid / 100 figure-8) and the channel-order swap ([21]) apply here -- both decoded from captures on this mic.

edge_note.notes: small-diaphragm pencil, matched-pair capable. Orion emuMic behaviour with this mic: untested.

edge_go.notes: USB modelling mic -- connects over USB, not an Orion XLR preamp, so the Orion emuMic path likely does not apply. Untested.

verge.notes: compact modelling mic, matched-pair capable. Orion emuMic behaviour with this mic: untested.

user_owned._comment: Set this per install. The repo owner (diafebus) has an Edge Duo; the 18-model list under `models` is that account's list as of 2026-08-31.
model_packs: (the 18 models in `models` -- exact pack breakdown unknown)

models._comment: model id ([20] in the 0x17/0xe5 frame) -> {name as shown in the Launcher, pattern_class}. The per-model `pattern_class` here is the DEFAULT polar-pattern index the Launcher presets on select (0/1/4) -- see the pattern_class block above for the 2026-09-01 correction, and pattern_index_ranges_2026_09_01 for each model's observed [22] range. Captured 2026-08-31 from 'emumic-model-select-...' on ONE account (an Edge Duo owner). WARNING: it is not confirmed whether these ids are GLOBAL (each model has a fixed id) or POSITIONAL (index into the list the Launcher shows YOU, which depends on which model packs you own). If positional, a user with a different pack set gets a different mapping. Treat this as that account's snapshot; a client should let the user pick by name. 'name' uses Antelope's own city+number naming (what the Launcher shows); the classic mics they emulate are deliberately not spelled out here (see account_binding.do_not).

0.name: EdgeDuo (raw / no emulation)
0.note: the mic's own sound; [22] is then the free 0-100 pattern morph
